title: This merge proposal will fix an issue with cp that made it incorrectly rewrite the permissions of its source target, resulting in behaviors such as the setuid bit being missing.
description:
This merge proposal will fix an issue with cp that made it incorrectly rewrite the permissions of its source target, resulting in behaviors such as the setuid bit being missing.

PPA: https://launchpad.net/~bamf0/+archive/ubuntu/rust-coreutils-lp2165041-missing-setuid-bit

diff --git a/debian/changelog b/debian/changelog
index a0ff86d..91890d3 100644
--- a/debian/changelog
+++ b/debian/changelog
@@ -1,3 +1,11 @@
+rust-coreutils (0.10.0-1ubuntu2) stonking; urgency=medium
+
+  * d/p/cp-fix-symlink-target-permissions.patch: Fix an issue where cp
+    would alter the permissions of the source file, such as stripping the
+    setuid bit (LP: #2165041)
+
+ -- Simon Johnsson <simon.johnsson@canonical.com>  Wed, 26 Aug 2026 16:29:49 +0200
+
 rust-coreutils (0.10.0-1ubuntu1) stonking; urgency=medium
 
   [ Simon Johnsson ]
diff --git a/debian/patches/cp-fix-symlink-target-permissions.patch b/debian/patches/cp-fix-symlink-target-permissions.patch
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..1534390
--- /dev/null
+++ b/debian/patches/cp-fix-symlink-target-permissions.patch
@@ -0,0 +1,71 @@
+From ab34a45c1981af9a65b712a5ecae2eb43b962979 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
+From: Angadi Yashaswini <angadi@digiscrypt.com>
+Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 20:40:44 +0530
+Subject: [PATCH] cp: decide the final chmod from the current destination state
+
+Drop the stale pre-copy dest_is_symlink from the guard and check
+dest.is_symlink() alone, as this line did before #6190. Besides not
+chmodding through a freshly copied symlink, this also applies the
+mode when --remove-destination replaces a symlink with a regular
+file, matching GNU cp.
+
+Origin: backport, https://github.com/uutils/coreutils/commit/ab34a45c1981af9a65b712a5ecae2eb43b962979.patch
+Bug: https://github.com/uutils/coreutils/issues/12191
+Bug-Ubuntu: https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/rust-coreutils/+bug/2165041
+---
+ src/uu/cp/src/cp.rs      | 12 ++++++------
+ tests/by-util/test_cp.rs | 26 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++
+ 2 files changed, 32 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)
+
+--- a/src/uu/cp/src/cp.rs
++++ b/src/uu/cp/src/cp.rs
+@@ -2682,8 +2682,12 @@ fn copy_file(
+         print_verbose_output(options.parents, progress_bar, source, dest)?;
+     }
+ 
+-    // TODO: implement something similar to gnu's lchown
+-    if !dest_is_symlink {
++    // Check the destination as it is now, not as it was before the copy:
++    // copying a symlink without dereferencing recreates it as a symlink here,
++    // and chmod() would follow it and change the mode of the link target,
++    // which can live outside the copied tree. Conversely, --remove-destination
++    // replaces a symlink with a regular file that still needs its mode set.
++    if !dest.is_symlink() {
+         // Here, to match GNU semantics, we quietly ignore an error
+         // if a user does not have the correct ownership to modify
+         // the permissions of a file.
+--- a/tests/by-util/test_cp.rs
++++ b/tests/by-util/test_cp.rs
+@@ -926,6 +926,32 @@ fn test_cp_arg_symlink() {
+     assert!(at.is_symlink(TEST_HELLO_WORLD_DEST));
+ }
+ 
++// With --remove-destination onto a symlink, cp removes the link and creates a
++// fresh regular file, so the final chmod must not be skipped based on the
++// destination's pre-copy symlink state. GNU cp gives the new file the source
++// mode masked by the umask (664 & ~022 = 644 here); skipping the chmod leaves
++// it at the restrictive 0o600 creation mode (or at the raw cloned source mode
++// on filesystems that copy via clonefile).
++#[test]
++#[cfg(unix)]
++fn test_cp_remove_destination_symlink_applies_mode() {
++    let (at, mut ucmd) = at_and_ucmd!();
++
++    at.touch("src");
++    at.set_mode("src", 0o664);
++    at.touch("target");
++    at.symlink_file("target", "dst");
++
++    ucmd.umask(0o022)
++        .arg("--remove-destination")
++        .arg("src")
++        .arg("dst")
++        .succeeds();
++
++    assert!(!at.is_symlink("dst"));
++    assert_eq!(at.metadata("dst").permissions().mode() & 0o777, 0o644);
++}
++
+ #[test]
+ fn test_cp_arg_no_clobber() {
+     let (at, mut ucmd) = at_and_ucmd!();

--- a/debian/patches/series
+++ b/debian/patches/series
@@ -18,3 +18,4 @@ require-utility-to-be-invoked-at-matching-path.patch
 dd-ensure-full-writes.patch
 rustix-use-libc-backend.patch
